newsitem.title: USA: Republican lawmaker opposes further Fed rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Republican lawmaker opposes further Fed rate hike.

text.p: A senior Republican lawmaker on Tuesday urged the Federal Reserve not to raise interest rates at its policy-setting meeting next week.
"There is no real evidence of inflation to justify Federal Reserve increases in interest rates," Rep. Jim Saxton, chairman of the Congressional Joint Economic Committee, said.

The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meets on May 20 to set interest rate policy. At its last meeting in March, it raised short-term rates by a quarter percentage point, a move Saxton said he opposed.

In remarks on the floor of the House of Representatives, the New Jersey Republican said he supported a goal of price stability for the Fed, but argued that the central bank should not act until it sees visible signs of inflation picking up.
"The Federal Reserve ... seems to view economic growth itself as inflationary," Saxton said. "I do not agree."
He also called for more openness at the Fed.

"If the Fed were clearer and more open about its conduct of monetary policy, a major source of market instability would be removed," Saxton said. "A more complete and timely release of FOMC minutes would be a big step in the right direction."
